old_text: It should be noted, especially in League and Saturday Matches, that Umpires are appointed “one for each end” and not one for each side.
new_text: It should be noted, especially in League and Saturday Matches, that Umpires are appointed “one for each end” and not one for each side. 6

old_text: The Bowling Crease shall be in a line with the stumps: six feet eight inches in length; the stumps in the centre; with a Return Crease at each end, at right angles behind the wicket.
new_text: The Bowling Crease shall be in a line with the stumps: eight feet eight inches in length; the stumps in the centre; with a Return Crease at each end, at right angles behind the wicket.

old_text: When part of the bowler’s foot is grounded on or outside the return crease the Umpire should call “No Ball.”
new_text: When part of the bowler’s foot is grounded on or outside the return crease the Umpire should call “NoBall.”

old_text: If he delivers with the heel raised off the ground and keeps that part of the foot which is on the ground within the return crease the delivery is allowed as fair.
new_text: If he delivers with the heel raised off the ground and keeps that part, of the foot which is on the ground within the return crease the delivery is allowed as fair.

old_text: Although not counted in the over No Balls and Wides arc recorded in their proper place on the score sheet.
new_text: Although not counted in the over No Balls and Wides are recorded in their proper place on the score sheet.

old_text: When a run is made by the bat off a “NoBall” only the run to the batsman should be scored and not the “No Ball” as well.
new_text: When a run is made by the bat off a “No Ball” only the run to the batsman should be scored and not the “No Ball” as well.

old_text: At the beginning of the match, and of each innings, the Umpire at the Bowler’s wicket shall call “Play”; from that time no trial ball shall be allowed to any bowler on the ground between the wickets, and when one of the batsmen is out, the use of the bat shall not be allowed to any person until the next batsman shall come in.
new_text: At the beginning of the match, and of each innings, the Umpire at the Bowler’s wicket shall call “Play”: from that time no trial ball shall be allowed to any bowler on the ground between the wickets, and when one of the batsmen is out, the use of the bat shall not be allowed to any person until the next batsman shall come in.

old_text: If the foot is on the line, but no part is within the batsman would be “out of his ground.”
new_text: If the foot is on the line, but no part is within, the batsman would be “out of his ground.”

old_text: If the batsman is in the act of jumping in the air and the bat is also off the ground he would be “out of his ground.”
new_text: If the batsman is in the act of jumping in the air and the bat is also off the ground he would be “out of his ground.” 9

old_text: If the wicket be bowled down, even if the ball first touch the Striker’s bat or person;—“ Bowled.”
new_text: If the wicket be bowled down, even if the ball first touch the Striker’s bat or person;—“Bowled.”

old_text: Or, if the ball, from a stroke of the bat or hand, but not the wrist, be held before it touch the ground, although it be hugged to the body of the catcher;—“ Caught.”
new_text: Or, if the ball, from a stroke of the bat or hand, but not the wrist, be held before it touch the ground, although it be hugged to the body of the catcher;—“Caught.”

old_text: If no boundaries have been arranged a Sinker can be caught off a tree, hedge, or building.
new_text: If no boundaries have been arranged a Striker can be caught off a tree, hedge, or building.

old_text: Or, if in playing at the ball, provided it be not touched by the bat or hand, the Striker be out of his ground, and the wicket be put down by the wicket-keeper with the ball, or with hand or arm with ball in hand;—“ Stumped.”
new_text: Or, if in playing at the ball, provided it be not touched by the bat or hand, the Striker be out of his ground, and the wicket be put down by the wicket-keeper with the ball, or with hand or arm with ball in hand “Stumped.”

old_text: If the ball rebounds off the pads or person of the wicket-keeper, without having first touched the bat or hand of the Striker, and the Striker is out of his ground the decision should be “Stumped,” and not “Run Out.”
new_text: If the ball rebounds off the pads or person of the wicket-keeper, without having first touched the bat or hand of the Striker, and the Striker is out of his ground the decision should be “Stumped,” and not “Run Out.” 10 It is sufficient for the wicket-keeper to remove one bail in order to run out or stump a batsman.

word_diff.new: 10 It is sufficient for the wicket-keeper to remove one bail in order to run out or stump a batsman.

old_text: A Batsman may be out l.b.w. although the bowler is bowling round the wicket, if the case comes within this Law.
new_text: A Batsman may be out lbw, although the bowler is bowling round the wicket, if the case comes within this Law.

old_text: It is sometimes only possible for a bowler bowling round the wicket to obtain an l.b.w. with a breaking ball.
new_text: It is sometimes only possible for a bowler bowling round the wicket to obtain an lbw with a breaking ball.

old_text: Or, if in playing at the ball he hit down his wicket with his bat or any part of his person or dress;—“ Hit Wicket.”
new_text: Or, if in playing at the ball he hit down his wicket with his bat or any part of his person or dress;—“Hit Wicket.”

old_text: Or, if under pretence of running, or otherwise, either of the batsmen wilfully prevent a ball from being caught;—“ Obstructing the field.”
new_text: Or, if under pretence of running, or otherwise, either of the batsmen wilfully prevent a ball from being caught;—“Obstructing the field.”

old_text: Or, if the ball be struck or be stopped by any part of his person, and he wilfully strike it again, except it be done for the purpose of guarding his wicket, which he may do with his bat, or any part of his person, except his hands;—“ Hit the ball twice.”
new_text: Or, if the ball be struck or be stopped by any part of his person, and he wilfully strike it again, except it be done for the purpose of guarding his wicket, which he may do with his bat, or any part of his person, except his hands;—“Hit the ball twice.” 11

old_text: If in running, or at any other time, when the ball is in play he be out of his ground, and his wicket be struck down by the ball after touching any fieldsman, or by the hand or arm, with ball in hand, of any fieldsman;—“ Run out.”
new_text: If in running, or at any other time, when the ball is in play he be out of his ground, and his wicket be struck down by the ball after touching any fieldsman, or by the hand or arm, with ball in hand, of any fieldsman;—“Run out.”

old_text: It would not be out if the striker hit the ball into the opposite wickets —the other batsman being out of his ground—unless the ball had been touched by a fieldsman after being hit and before striking the wickets.
new_text: It would not be out if the striker hit the ball into the opposite wickets—the other batsman being out of his ground—unless the ball had been touched by a fieldsman after being hit and before striking the wickets.

old_text: Or, if he touch with his hands or take up the ball while in play, unless at the request of the opposite side;—“ Handled the ball.”
new_text: Or, if he touch with his hands or take up the ball while in play, unless at the request of the opposite side;—“Handled the ball.”

old_text: Or, if he wilfully obstruct any Fieldsman;—“ Obstructing the field.”
new_text: Or, if he wilfully obstruct any Fieldsman;—“Obstructing the field.”

old_text: (Sec Notes on Law 22.)
new_text: (See Notes on Law’ 22.)

old_text: Although that run which is being attempted shall not be scored it is not the custom for the remaining batsman to resume his position at the wicket he has left if he and his partner have crossed.
new_text: Although that run which is being attempted shall not be scored it is not the custom for the remaining batsman to resume his position at the wicket he has left if he and his partner have crossed. 12

old_text: A Batsman being out from any cause, the ball shall be “Dead.”
new_text: A Batsman being out from any cause, the ball shall be “Dead”

old_text: A ball does not become “Dead” when the bails are off or the wickets struck down or because an unsuccessful appeal has been made. to the Umpire.
new_text: A ball does not become “Dead” when the bails are off or the wickets struck down or because an unsuccessful appeal has been made to the Umpire.

old_text: If a ball in play cannot be found or recovered, any Fieldsman may call “Lost Ball” when the ball shall be “Dead”; six runs shall be added to the score; but if more than six runs have been run before “Lost Ball” has been called, as many runs as have been run shall be scored.
new_text: If a ball in play cannot be found or recovered, any Fieldsman may call “Lost Ball,” when the ball shall be “Dead”; six runs shall be added to the score; but if more than six runs have been run before “Lost Ball” has been called, as many runs as have been run shall be scored.

old_text: After the ball shall have been finally settled in the Wicket-keeper’s or Bowler’s hand, it shall be “Dead”; but when the Bowler is about to deliver the ball, if the Batsman at his wicket be out of his ground before actual delivery, the said Bowler may run him out: but if the Bowler throw at that wicket and any run result, it shall be scored “No Ball.”
new_text: After the ball shall have been finally settled in the Wicketkeeper’s or Bowler’s hand, it shall be “Dead”; but when the Bowler is about to deliver the ball, if the Batsman at his wicket be out of his ground before actual delivery, the said Bowler may run him out; but if the Bowler throw at that wicket and any run result, it shall be scored “No Ball.”

old_text: A bowler may run a Batsman out, without having delivered the ball, in anyway authorized by the Laws, he may have passed the bowling crease in his run or may change the ball from one hand to the other before throwing at the wicket or knocking off the bails.
new_text: He may have passed the howling crease in his run or may change the ball from one hand to the other before throwing at the wicket or knocking off the bails.

old_text: The Umpires are the sole judges of fair or unfair play, of the fitness of the ground, the weather, and the light for play: all disputes shall be determined by them, and if they disagree the actual state of things shall continue.
new_text: The Umpires are the sole judges of fair or unfair play, of the fitness of the ground, the weather, and the light for play; all disputes, shall be determined by them, and if they disagree the actual state of things shall continue.

new_text: (See also Instructions to Umpires.)

old_text: N.B.—An appeal, “How’s that?” covers all ways of being out (within the jurisdiction of the Umpire appealed to), unless a specific way of getting out is stated by the person asking.
new_text: N.B.—An appeal, “How’s that?” covers all ways of being out (within the jurisdiction of the Umpire appealed to), unless a specific way of getting out is stated by the person .asking.

old_text: The In-side may declare their innings at an end in a three days’ match, at or after the luncheon interval on the second day; in a two days’ match on the second day, at any time; in a one day match at any time.
new_text: The In-side may declare their innings at an end in a three days’ match, at or after the luncheon interval on the second day; in a two days’ match the Captain of the batting side has power to declare his innings at a close at any time; but such declaration may not be made on the first day later than 1 hour and 40 minutes before the hour agreed on for drawing stumps; in a one day match at any time.
